It swallows; only the log line remains. That's per design. But notice: after the breaker trips, the notice is never delivered again for that key even after... revision change re-arms. OK. Timer/RAF wrapping: `setTimeout = function(fn, ms) { return baseSetTimeout(__wrapCb(fn), ms); }` — In strict-mode JS runtimes, assigning to undeclared `setTimeout` may throw in strict mode, and importantly, if the runtime's setTimeout is a global binding that is non-writable (like in some JS engines / Hermes / QuickJS where globals are const), assignment throws ReferenceError/TypeError. What about locale containing a literal newline? `'en\n...'` — a newline inside a single-quoted JS string literal is a syntax error, breaking the whole bootstrap. Not an injection (no escaping context), but a syntax error. Realistically languageCode can't contain newlines. Minor.

A Flutter package that runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native Flutter UI.

- **VM/desktop/mobile**: uses [`flutter_js`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_js) (QuickJS / JavaScriptCore).
- **Web**: uses a dedicated `web.Worker` spawned from an inline Blob URL.
- **Opt-in QuickJS FFI backend** (VM only): swap `flutter_js` for the [quickjs_runtime](https://pub.dev/packages/quickjs_runtime) package to get fully synchronous host calls — build the native library with `bash <quickjs_runtime>/tool/build_quickjs.sh`, then pass `QuickjsWidgetEngineBackend` via `JsRuntimeConfig.backend`.

The JS side communicates with Flutter through a declarative JSON UI tree and a small async bridge (`render`, `fetchJson`, `exec`, `storage`, `secrets`, timers, `requestAnimationFrame`, etc.).

**[▶ Live demos](https://istin.github.io/flutter_js_widget_runtime/)** — click through the widget gallery in your browser: each demo runs in the real engine (Web Worker backend) on GitHub Pages.

## Web preview runner

`example/lib/preview.dart` is a web-only entry point that renders a single widget full-bleed through the real engine (Web Worker backend) — built for hosting live widget previews behind an iframe:

```
cd example && flutter build web -t lib/preview.dart --base-href /widgets/preview/
```

URL contract: `?widget=<id>&theme=dark|light`, with widget files fetched over HTTP (`?base=<url>` to override the source). `fetch` is enabled only for widgets whose manifest opts into `"network": true`. CI (`.github/workflows/preview-web.yml`) publishes the build as the `jsr-preview-web` artifact.

The runner also powers the **live demo site on GitHub Pages** — https://istin.github.io/flutter_js_widget_runtime/ — deployed by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: a landing page (`site/index.html`, widget cards built from the fa_widgets catalog) at the root plus the runner under `/preview/` (base-href `/flutter_js_widget_runtime/preview/`).

## Quick start

```
flutter pub add js_widget_runtime
```

```
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:js_widget_runtime/js_widget_runtime.dart';

class DemoPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const DemoPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return JsWidgetRuntime(
      jsSource: r'''
(function() {
  jsr.render({
    type: 'center',
    child: {
      type: 'column',
      mainAxisSize: 'min',
      children: [
        {type: 'text', data: 'Hello from JS!', style: {fontSize: 24}},
        {type: 'sizedBox', height: 12},
        {
          type: 'textButton',
          text: 'Tap me',
          onTap: 'tap',
        },
      ],
    },
  });
  jsr.onEvent(function(actionId, payload) {
    if (actionId === 'tap') {
      jsr.setTitle('Tapped!');
    }
  });
})();
''',
      runtimeConfig: JsRuntimeConfig(
        onRender: (tree) => print('render: $tree'),
        onSetTitle: (title) => print('title: $title'),
        onStorageUpdate: (storage) => print('storage: $storage'),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

See the `example/` folder for a runnable menu of sample JS apps.

## 3D scenes and GLB models

`js_widget_runtime` does not bundle a 3D engine. Instead it exposes a `Js3dHost` interface so the host app can plug in any engine (Flame 3D, three_dart, `flutter_3d_controller`, etc.).

```
JsRuntimeConfig(
  js3dHost: const My3dHost(),
  // ... other handlers
);
```

From JS, create a scene and manipulate it:

```
jsr.scene3d.create('main', {
  camera: { position: [0, 2, 5], target: [0, 0, 0] },
  lights: [{ type: 'ambient', color: '#ffffff', intensity: 0.5 }]
});

jsr.render({
  type: 'scene3d',
  id: 'main',
  width: 320,
  height: 320
});

jsr.scene3d.addModel('main', {
  id: 'player',
  src: 'assets/player.glb'
});

jsr.scene3d.playAnimation('main', 'player', 'run');

jsr.scene3d.setTransform('main', 'player', {
  position: [1, 0, 0],
  rotation: [0, 45, 0],
  scale: [1.5, 1.5, 1.5]
});
```

The `example/` app includes a `3d-viewer` widget powered by `flutter_3d_controller`.

## Renderer nodes

The JSON tree supports these node types:

 <markdown-accessiblity-table>

|  Category |  Nodes |
| --- | --- |

|  Layout |  `column`, `row`, `stack`, `center`, `padding`, `sizedBox`, `expanded`, `flexible`, `wrap`, `align`, `absoluteFill` |

|  Display |  `text`, `icon`, `markdown`, `divider`, `spacer`, `image`, `svg`, `avatar`, `chip`, `badge`, `path`, progress indicators |

|  Container |  `container`, `card`, `inkWell`, `safeArea`, `scroll`, `blur` |

|  List |  `listView`, `gridView`, `listTile`. Scrolling is configurable: `shrinkWrap` (default `true`) and `physics` (`'never'` / `'always'` / `'platform'`; default `'always'` for `listView`, `'never'` for `gridView`). Use `shrinkWrap: false` in a bounded parent to let the view scroll |

|  Input |  `button`, `textButton`, `outlinedButton`, `iconButton`, `textField`, `textArea` (multiline input: `value`, `hint`, `minLines` default 3, `maxLines` default 8, `onChange` per keystroke, optional `onSubmit` done action), `switch`, `checkbox`, `slider`, `dropdown` |

|  Animation |  `animatedContainer`, `animatedOpacity`, `animatedPositioned` (implicit change animations); `entrance` — one-shot mount animation (`animation`: `fade`/`slideUp`/`slideDown`/`slideLeft`/`slideRight`/`scale`/`fadeScale`, `delay` ms for staggered lists, `duration`, `curve`); `animatedSwitcher` — view transition when `switchKey` changes (`animation`: `fade`/`slideLeft`/`slideRight`/`slideUp`/`scale`/`fadeScale`) |

|  Map |  `map` — OpenStreetMap via [flutter_map](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_map) (no API key). Props: `center {lat, lng}`, `zoom`, `markers [{id, lat, lng, label?, color?}]`, `polylines [{points, color?, width?}]`, `fitBounds`; events: `onTap` (`{lat, lng}`), `onMarkerTap` (`{id}`) |

|  Chart |  `chart` — sparkline or bar chart. Props: `data` (list of numbers; `points` accepted as alias), `chartType` (`line` default, `bar`), `color`, `fillColor` (hex with alpha, e.g. `#22c55e33`), `strokeWidth`, `height` |

|  3D |  `scene3d` — host-provided 3D engine. Props: `id`, `width`, `height`, `camera`, `lights`. GLB/GLTF models, cameras and lights are controlled from JS via `jsr.scene3d.*` |

|  Media |  `video`, `audio` (host-provided via `JsMediaHost`) |

|  Gestures |  `gestureDetector` |

</markdown-accessiblity-table>

## Features

- Cross-platform JS execution (VM + web).
- Declarative JSON-to-Flutter renderer with layout, input, animation and gesture nodes.
- Effects ported from YoClip: radial gradients, box shadows, blur, 3D transforms, clip, text shadows.
- `manifest.json` based app registry with example widgets.
- Injected I/O handlers so the host controls permissions (network, CLI, secure storage).
- Host-specific JS APIs via `JsRuntimeConfig.hostBootstrapJs` (e.g., `jsr.yoloit = {...}`).
- Default in-memory handlers for demo/development use.

## Review: JS app error reporting path (gh-1164 Part B)

Findings ordered by severity. (Not re-reporting the two diagnosed CI failures.)

### BLOCKING

1. **Every `AgentService` subscribes to the global channel and `_onJsAppError` ignores `notice.appId` — one app error spawns a system-notice turn in ALL live sessions.** `_withEnv` subscribes unconditionally at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:716-718`, and `_onJsAppError` (`agent_service_inbox.dart:94-111`) does no app→session routing or filtering. `FlutterSessionManager` explicitly "owns several concurrent `AgentService` instances … without aborting in-flight work" (`flutter_session_manager.dart:18-20`). With 2+ sessions alive, a single gated notice is delivered as a `<system-notice>` user message (→ an LLM turn) in every session, including unrelated main-chat sessions — duplicated cost and cross-session noise, and it contradicts the channel's own contract ("exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes `onDeliver` and routes notices into the app-bound session", `js_app_error_channel.dart` class doc; also `publish`'s hasListener semantics at `js_app_error_channel.dart:157-163`). Needs an appId→bound-session map or single-owner routing.

### IMPORTANT

2. **Engine boot failures never reach the channel; `JsAppErrorKind.bootstrap` has no emitter.** `JsAppView._restart`'s catch (`js_app_view.dart:344-347`) only sets `_startError` for the UI. Failures like the platform-unsupported `StateError` thrown in `JsAppEngine._start` *before any engine exists* (`js_app_engine.dart:335-337`), `engine.run()` throws not routed through `jsr.showError`, or manifest errors caught before engine construction, are never `reportHostError`'d — yet the `bootstrap` kind exists in `js_app_errors.dart:36-37` and is parsed in `fromLogJson`. This is exactly the "engine failed to start at all" case the enum was added for; it silently drops the feedback loop gh-1164 exists to create.

3. **`sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces double-report.** `js_app_engine.dart:349` (`sha256('$entryFile\n$js')`). Consequences: (a) apps load other source via `loadAsset` — an agent fix to a non-entry file leaves the revision unchanged, so after the circuit breaker trips, the recurring error stays silenced forever (the "an edit re-arms everything" contract in `js_app_error_channel.dart:135-139` only holds for the entry); (b) the revision includes the entry *name*, so the tile engine and the fullscreen engine of one app hash differently and the same runtime error is delivered twice, contradicting "one report per (app, error fingerprint)" (`js_app_errors.dart:11-14`). The view's `_readAppSignature` (`js_app_view.dart:258-272`) has the same entry-only limitation for reloads.

4. **The bootstrap never emits `fingerprint` (and no JS-side hard cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.** `__faReport` (`js_app_engine.dart:858-868`) sends only `kind/message/stack`; `JsAppErrorEvent.dedupKey` (`js_app_errors.dart:78-82`) then falls back to `message + first stack line`. A per-frame error whose message embeds varying data (`'frame error ' + n` — the shape `js_app_error_capture_test.dart:88-96` itself uses) produces a new key per occurrence, each delivered once; the circuit breaker never trips because it's per-key. The class doc promises "[fingerprint] dedups bursts" and "stack … already truncated by the reporter in JS where a hard cap matters" (`js_app_errors.dart:12-14`) — neither is implemented; the raw unbounded stack also crosses the bridge on every frame (Dart caps only the *notice*, `js_app_error_channel.dart:177-190`).

5. **`reportHostError` misses the render errors it was built for.** `js_app_view.dart:816-826` wraps only `renderer.build(tree, context)` — JSON→Widget *conversion*. Flutter "red screen" errors are thrown later, during element inflation/layout of the returned tree, outside this try/catch, so they're never reported to the agent. Either hook `FlutterError.onError`/an `ErrorBoundary`, or scope the comment/claim to conversion errors only.

### SUGGESTION

6. **Misleading boilerplate on every notice** — `agent_service_inbox.dart:103-107`: "The app source changed since a previous identical report may have been silenced" is appended even to the *first* delivery of a key, asserting something unverified. Reword or gate on `notice` repeat state.

7. **Locale interpolation into the bootstrap strips only `'`** — `js_app_engine.dart:742-746` (`faBootstrapJsFor`). Not injectable (the breakout char is removed) but a locale containing a newline/U+2028 yields a JS syntax error killing the *entire* host bootstrap (all `jsr.fa.*` bridges + error capture). Use `jsonEncode(locale)`. (Verified: app source is executed via `engine.run` and never string-inlined, so quotes/newlines in app code or file paths cannot break the bootstrap — no injection there.)

8. **Error-capture IIFE assigns globals with no per-leg guard** — `js_app_engine.dart:878-894`: `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` reassignment and `window.onerror =`/`onunhandledrejection =` run unguarded. One throwing assignment (read-only global in some engine configs) aborts the remaining legs (including the `onerror` leg) and can escape the bootstrap eval; assigning `window.onerror` also clobbers any pre-existing handler — `addEventListener('error'/'unhandledrejection')` composes instead.

9. **Marker spoofing** — `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` (`js_app_error_channel.dart:27-40`) accepts any console line containing `faAppError:{json}`: app code can forge error notices into the agent session (dedup-capped but unauthenticated). Low impact (apps already have `emit`/LLM channels), but worth documenting or namespacing.

10. **Smoke-gate error collector unbounded** — `app_preflight.dart:~113`: `errors.add(...)` for the full 10 s budget with only `errors.first` ever used; a throw-per-frame app accumulates thousands of entries. Cap the list.

### Checked and OK
- Revision is captured at event time correctly (hash of the booting entry, set before `engine.run` at `js_app_engine.dart:349`, read at report time in `_forwardError:445-467`).
- Circuit breaker semantics are intentional: first occurrence delivers, repeats 2–5 return `deliver:false`, then `null` — still a raw log line, not fully silent (`js_app_error_channel.dart:135-153`).
- Payload bounding is correct (message 500, 5 frames/800 chars stack, truncation marked; test asserts < 2000 chars).
- No listener leaks: `AgentService.dispose` cancels `_jsAppErrorSub` (`agent_service.dart` dispose); preflight's `_awaitFirstRender` removes its `tree` listener on both paths (`app_preflight.dart:204-224`); engines push into the channel without subscribing.
- Reentrancy is safe: the broadcast controller is async-by-default, so `_onJsAppError`→`sendText` runs in a later microtask, never inside the engine-log callback or a build; mid-run delivery correctly steers, idle delivery starts a fresh turn.
